facts.statement: Weewarrasaurus is classified as a genus of ornithopod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Weewarrasaurus is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur

facts.statement: Weewarrasaurus belongs to the suborder Neornithischia and the infraorder Ornithopoda within the order Ornithischia.
facts.quote: superordo: Dinosauria ordo: Ornithischia subordo: Neornithischia infraordo: Ornithopoda

facts.statement: Weewarrasaurus lived during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 100 to 93 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivó a mediados del período Cretácico hace aproximadamente entre 100 y 93 millones de años durante el Cenomaniense

facts.statement: The fossil record for Weewarrasaurus spans from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Weewarrasaurus have been found in the Griman Creek Formation near Lightning Ridge, New South Wales, Australia.
facts.quote: from the Late Cretaceous of the Griman Creek Formation near Lightning Ridge, in New South Wales, Australia

facts.statement: The type specimen of Weewarrasaurus was first discovered in 2013 by miners.
facts.quote: It was first discovered in 2013 by miners

facts.statement: Paleontologist Phil Bell examined the specimen in 2014 and recognized its scientific importance.
facts.quote: Palaeontologist Phil Bell was shown the specimen in 2014 and remarked upon its significance

facts.statement: The genus name Weewarrasaurus combines the Wee Warra fossil locality with the Greek word saurus, meaning lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name Weewarrasaurus refers to the Wee Warra fossil locality where the fossils were found, and the Greek word saurus, meaning lizard

facts.statement: The species name W. pobeni honors Mike Poben, the opal dealer who first identified the fossil.
facts.quote: The specific name, W. pobeni, honours Poben

facts.statement: The holotype fossil is notable for being preserved in green-blue opal.
facts.quote: The specimen was noted for being preserved in green-blue opal, a gemstone for which the region is well known

facts.statement: A second partial jawbone, specimen LRF 766, was referred to the species based on similar tooth morphology.
facts.quote: In addition to the opal type specimen, or holotype, the researchers assigned a second partial jawbone, specimen LRF 766, to the new species, due to the similar tooth morphology

facts.statement: Weewarrasaurus likely co-existed with various other ornithopods of different sizes and evolutionary lineages.
facts.quote: It is thought to have co-existed with multiple other ornithopods of different sizes and lineages

facts.statement: Weewarrasaurus is the only known species in the extinct elasmarian ornithopod genus.
facts.quote: es la única especie conocida del género extinto Weewarrasaurus de dinosaurio ornitópodo elasmariano

facts.statement: Natural opal banding patterns allowed researchers to confirm that the two broken jaw sections belonged to the same individual.
facts.quote: The opal banding on the fossil was used to confirm that both parts of the dentary, which do not form a continuous sequence, were from the same individual

rejected.quote: Bell and colleagues later named it as a new genus and species in a study published on December 4, 2018
